messages.subject: Re: Nimble error

Hi Matthew,

Yes, as Andrew says, it looks like there are NA or NaN values
appearing in some iterations of the MCMC.

If you use runMCMC() instead of nimbleMCMC() (there is documentation
in the manual or with help(runMCMC)),
you should be able to get the posterior samples and look for NAs and
try to get a sense for what is going wrong.
It may be caused by bad starting values or some sort of numerical
issue (e.g, numerical underflow or overflow).

We're just now working on making reversible jump for variable
selection available in NIMBLE. If you can provide
a reproducible example we could look more closely to see what might be
going wrong. You could share that
with us privately by just emailing me directly.

Chris
